description: Topic-comment fronting correction (audit commit ad3641395), rule en-l4-topic-comment-word-order. Vietnamese learners front the topic ('This book I like'); the rule re-orders the three audited surfaces to canonical SVO. expectedCorrection / expectedStatus encode the VERIFIED output of correctWithTutorRules('en') on current main (captured from the live engine, not hand-traced): the engine normalizes whitespace, capitalizes only the first character, runs the rule loop, then adds terminal punctuation. The rule is exact-match on its 3 audited surfaces, so positives are meaningful variants across those surfaces (case / trailing punctuation / optional comma).
fp_risk_note: Topic-comment fronting is the 2nd-highest false-positive surface in the audit set: the same comma-fronted, object-first shape that signals awkward learner English is ALSO valid English emphasis. The negative cases stress: (1) valid topicalization with a resumptive pronoun — 'My homework, I finished it'; (2) conditional fronting — 'If it rains, we cancel'; (3) adverbial fronting — 'Slowly, she opened the door'; (4) ESL question-word fronting — 'What time, did you arrive?'; (5) quoted speech with an internal comma — "'Yes,' he said"; (6) prepositional-phrase fronting, including the deliberate near-miss of the 'In my family,...' positive prefix — 'In the morning, I exercise' (PP preamble but NO fronted object); (7) subordinate-clause fronting — 'Because I was tired, I slept early'. A regression that widens the rule from its 3 hardcoded surfaces toward a general fronting detector will start rewriting these valid sentences — any such change must re-green this negative set first.
